cohort: 1,624,744 non-Hispanic Black women who gave birth between 2017 and 2019 in the United States
finding: Among non-Hispanic Black women, the three factors most strongly associated with severe maternal morbidity were cesarean delivery, earlier gestational age at delivery, and preeclampsia.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was the factor most strongly associated with severe maternal morbidity among non-Hispanic Black women.
gest_age: Live births greater than 23 weeks of gestation
